newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to push "Buy Russian" campaign - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to push "Buy Russian" campaign - Tass.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will use his regular radio address to the nation on Tuesday to give a boost to his newly launched "buy Russian" campaign, Itar-Tass news agency quoted the Kremlin as saying on Monday.

Yeltsin's press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky was quoted as saying the president would lay out the reasons behind a call to buy Russian-produced goods he first made on Friday. The Kremlin press office was not immediately available for comment.

Yeltsin, worried by a continuing decline of Russian industry, appealed in his televised address on Friday to millions of Russians asking them to turn their attention to competitive goods produced at home.

"I want to put the following idea to the people of Russia: the situation in our country is such that our markets are full to overflowing with foreign goods, even though our enterprises and organisations are capable of producing goods, many goods, which are just as good or even better," Yeltsin said.
The 66-year-old president, who recently ordered officials to switch from foreign to Russian cars, made clear that his "Buy Russian" campaign would not mean restrictions on imports.
"We have freedom now and there is no question of any sort of shortage of foreign goods -- there won't be any less of them just because I have made this address to you," he said.
